variants.title: Size the cache
variants.context: The target is 1.5 million operations per second with an 80/20 read-write mix, a 2 TB working set, RF=2, and 48 GB usable memory per node.
variants.prompt: 1.5 million operations per second with 80% reads. How many reads per second?
variants.explanation: 1.5M × 0.80 = 1.2M reads per second; writes are the remaining 300K.

variants.title: Size the cache
variants.context: The target is 1.5 million operations per second with an 80/20 read-write mix, a 2 TB working set, RF=2, and 48 GB usable memory per node.
variants.prompt: 1.2 million reads per second at a 90% hit rate. How many reads per second reach the origin?
variants.hint: Multiply reads by the miss rate.
variants.explanation: 1.2M × 0.10 = 120K origin reads per second; the origin must survive that plus a recovery surge.

variants.title: Size the cache
variants.context: The target is 1.5 million operations per second with an 80/20 read-write mix, a 2 TB working set, RF=2, and 48 GB usable memory per node.
variants.prompt: A 2 TB working set with RF=2 on nodes with 48 GB usable memory each. What is the memory-only node floor?
variants.hint: Double the working set, then divide by usable memory and round up.
variants.explanation: 2 TB × 2 = 4,000 GB; 4,000 ÷ 48 = 83.3, so 84 nodes before skew, failure, and rebalancing headroom.

mistakes.feedback: Round up; 83 nodes hold less than 4 TB.

variants.title: State the cache contract
variants.context: A distributed cache is not authoritative storage. Decide which values may be stale or lost, which namespaces need read-your-writes, and what happens when the cache is unavailable. No cross-key transactions; values above 1 MB belong elsewhere.
variants.prompt: A value exists only in the cache and nowhere else. What is this system?
options: A database with a durability problem, not a cache; it needs a different review.
optionFeedback: Is the cache disposable? If not, it is authoritative storage.
variants.hint: What happens if the value is lost?
variants.explanation: Locks, balances, and durable counters remain outside the cache contract.

variants.title: State the cache contract
variants.context: A distributed cache is not authoritative storage. Decide which values may be stale or lost, which namespaces need read-your-writes, and what happens when the cache is unavailable. No cross-key transactions; values above 1 MB belong elsewhere.
variants.prompt: Session state must be read back immediately after it is written in the same region. Which promise?
options: Read-your-writes within the serving region for the session namespace.
optionFeedback: Derived objects may tolerate 100 ms; sessions may not.
variants.hint: What is the staleness budget for this namespace?
variants.explanation: State one namespace contract at a time.

variants.title: State the cache contract
variants.context: A distributed cache is not authoritative storage. Decide which values may be stale or lost, which namespaces need read-your-writes, and what happens when the cache is unavailable. No cross-key transactions; values above 1 MB belong elsewhere.
variants.prompt: A client wants to update two keys atomically. What does the contract say?
options: No cross-key transaction guarantee; design around single-key operations or use another system.
optionFeedback: Cross-key atomicity is out of scope.
MGET groups reads; it is not a transaction.
A lock key in the cache is not a durable lock.
variants.hint: Which operations does the cache promise?
variants.explanation: GET, SET, DELETE, and MGET with per-key results.

variants.title: Bound the miss
variants.context: A miss must not become an unlimited request to the backing store: request coalescing, origin admission limits, TTL jitter, and stale-value policies bound the miss path.
variants.prompt: A popular key expires and ten thousand requests miss at once. Which control prevents ten thousand origin reads?
options: Request coalescing so one origin read serves the waiting requests.
optionFeedback: Capacity is not the fix for a stampede.
variants.hint: How many origin reads does one missing key deserve?

variants.title: Bound the miss
variants.context: A miss must not become an unlimited request to the backing store: request coalescing, origin admission limits, TTL jitter, and stale-value policies bound the miss path.
variants.prompt: Thousands of keys were written at the same second and will expire together. Which control helps?
options: TTL jitter so expirations spread out.
variants.hint: When do these keys expire relative to each other?

variants.title: Bound the miss
variants.context: A miss must not become an unlimited request to the backing store: request coalescing, origin admission limits, TTL jitter, and stale-value policies bound the miss path.
variants.prompt: The cache tier fails entirely. What protects the origin?
options: Origin admission limits with a defined degraded response, and stale serving where allowed.
optionFeedback: Cache loss must not become an origin outage.
Unbounded fallback is the failure mode.
variants.hint: What is the origin fallback budget?
variants.explanation: Define origin deadlines, retry budgets, and degradation before choosing software.

variants.title: Own the key
variants.context: For one ring version, each key has deterministic primary ownership. Fenced ownership, gradual range movement, replica promotion, and warm-up controls make membership changes observable and reversible.
variants.prompt: Two nodes both believe they own a key range during a migration. Which control prevents conflicting writes?
options: Fenced ownership tied to the ring version.
optionFeedback: Only one owner per ring version, enforced by fencing.
Speed reduces the window but does not close it.
variants.hint: What proves which node owns the range now?
variants.explanation: Membership changes must be observable and reversible.

variants.title: Own the key
variants.context: For one ring version, each key has deterministic primary ownership. Fenced ownership, gradual range movement, replica promotion, and warm-up controls make membership changes observable and reversible.
variants.prompt: Replicas of a shard sit on the same host. What is wrong?
options: They share a failure unit; place replicas across hosts, racks, or zones.
They should be on the same rack for speed.
optionFeedback: Replicas on the same host do not protect against that host failing.
Two copies in one failure domain is one copy.

variants.title: Own the key
variants.context: For one ring version, each key has deterministic primary ownership. Fenced ownership, gradual range movement, replica promotion, and warm-up controls make membership changes observable and reversible.
variants.prompt: A new node joins and immediately takes its full share of traffic. What is the risk?
options: Its cache is cold, so its misses surge at the origin; use warm-up controls and gradual range movement.
It will run out of memory.
optionFeedback: Memory is not the immediate issue.
variants.hint: What is the hit rate of an empty node?

variants.title: Prevent revival
variants.context: Versions and tombstones prevent delayed replicas from reviving old values. DELETE carries a version so it cannot revive an older write.
variants.prompt: A delayed replica applies an old SET after a newer DELETE. What prevents the old value from coming back?
options: Versions and tombstones: the delete carries a version that rejects the older write.
optionFeedback: Versioned deletes cannot revive old values.
variants.hint: Which write is newer, and how does the replica know?
variants.explanation: DELETE(key, version) invalidates without reviving an older write.

variants.title: Prevent revival
variants.context: Versions and tombstones prevent delayed replicas from reviving old values. DELETE carries a version so it cannot revive an older write.
variants.prompt: A 3 MB object is being cached. What does the contract say?
options: Values above 1 MB belong in object storage or a CDN, not this cache.
optionFeedback: Large values are out of scope.
Compression does not change the contract.
variants.hint: What is the value size bound?

variants.title: Prevent revival
variants.context: Versions and tombstones prevent delayed replicas from reviving old values. DELETE carries a version so it cannot revive an older write.
variants.prompt: After a node failure, a replica is promoted. What must the promotion preserve?
options: The ring version and versioned values so stale writes cannot win after promotion.
optionFeedback: Promotion is a membership change with the same fencing rules.
variants.hint: What could an old write do after promotion?
variants.explanation: Replica promotion is part of the ownership contract.
